notes: §1985:IV.4.3.8.4.3 SR5 (Amendment 1): "The function referenced by function-name-1 and its arguments, if any, must be an alphanumeric function." ResultRefMod, the one applier of a reference-modifier to a function result (reached from FinishIntrinsic), decides from the bound call's result category, which the arguments set for MAX and MIN, and refuses a numeric or integer function with COBOL1629; the national and boolean categories it also admits name no function at 85, because BindFunctionResult refuses every function introduced after the 1989 module with COBOL1502. Probed at 85: MAX (A1 A2) (2:3) over alphanumeric items is accepted and MAX (N1 N2) (1:1) over numeric items is refused, as are LENGTH, SQRT, NUMVAL and INTEGER-OF-DATE; a second modifier on the result draws COBOL1630. The witness accepts UPPER-CASE (WS-A) (2:2) and refuses ORD (WS-B (1:1)) (1:1).

next.reason: 1985 (syntax rule 5 comes from Amendment 1, X3.23a-1989): "The function referenced by function-name-1 and its arguments, if any, must be an alphanumeric function" (§1985:IV.4.3.8.4.3 SR5). 2023: "If identifier-1 is a function-identifier, it shall reference an alphanumeric, boolean, or national function" (§2023:8.4.3.3.3 SR2). The words that differ are "alphanumeric, boolean, or national": 2023 also accepts reference modification of a boolean or national function, which the 1985 rule refuses. A numeric or integer function is refused by both.
